question: Which hormones are the main drivers of body changes and metabolism during pregnancy?
explanation: Hormones like human placental lactogen, progesterone, and estrogen drive the metabolic shifts seen in pregnant women. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why does body metabolism change significantly during pregnancy and breastfeeding?

options.A: To prevent the digestion of dietary proteins
options.B: To support fetal growth and milk production
options.C: To speed up the resting heart rate of the mother
options.D: To completely eliminate maternal fat stores

explanation: The body adapts its nutrient handling to meet the high energetic demands of the growing fetus and subsequent lactation. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the main sugar circulating in the blood that gives cells quick energy?
explanation: Glucose is the main sugar used by the body's cells for quick energy production. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h2)

question: What happens to the mother's response to insulin in late pregnancy?

options.A: Insulin sensitivity decreases to keep more sugar for the baby
options.B: Insulin sensitivity increases to clear blood sugar rapidly
options.C: All blood sugar is turned into muscle protein
options.D: The pancreas stops making insulin completely

explanation: Late pregnancy insulin resistance leaves more glucose available in the maternal blood for placental transfer. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h2)

question: Where does the body store extra dietary protein for long-term emergency use?

options.A: The body does not have a dedicated protein storage depot
options.B: Fat tissue converts it into stored albumin
options.C: Skeletal muscles store it as dense amino acid crystals
options.D: The liver stores it as specialized protein granules

explanation: Unlike fats and carbohydrates, amino acids are not stored for later use and must be continuously supplied or recycled. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h3)

question: What happens to the nitrogen part when extra amino acids are broken down for energy?

options.A: It is stored in bones to make them stronger
options.B: It is turned into urea and passed out in the urine
options.C: It is turned directly into stored muscle starch
options.D: It is breathed out through the lungs as nitrogen gas

explanation: Liver deamination removes the toxic amine group, turning it into urea so the kidneys can safely flush it out. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which food group gives the most stored energy gram for gram?
explanation: Lipids yield more than double the calories per gram compared to carbohydrates and proteins. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h4)

question: When does the liver produce higher amounts of ketone bodies?

options.A: When carbohydrate availability is very low
options.B: When protein breakdown rates exceed normal limits
options.C: Right after eating a heavy carbohydrate meal
options.D: When blood sugar levels are extremely high

explanation: Low carbohydrate availability forces the body to rely heavily on fat breakdown, leading to elevated ketone production. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which key molecule connects the breakdown pathways of carbs, proteins, and fats?
explanation: Acetyl-CoA is the key entry intermediate that feeds directly into the Krebs cycle for energy generation. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h5)

question: How does the body handle extra carbohydrates when energy needs are already met?

options.A: It destroys them through kidney filtration
options.B: It passes them out through sweat glands
options.C: It stores them as free amino acids in the blood
options.D: It turns them into fat for storage

explanation: Excess carbs that are not needed for immediate energy or glycogen storage are shifted into lipogenesis and stored as fat. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h5)

question: How does glucose mainly cross the placenta to reach the baby?
explanation: Glucose moves across the placenta down a concentration gradient using specialized carrier proteins. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main reason metabolism shifts from storing nutrients early in pregnancy to breaking them down late in pregnancy?

options.A: To cause the mother to develop gestational diabetes
options.B: To ensure a steady fuel supply to the growing baby
options.C: To completely empty fat reserves before delivery
options.D: To stop amino acids from reaching the baby

explanation: Accelerated late pregnancy catabolism ensures the fetus gets steady nutrients even when the mother is fasting. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T4#BMP121_U2_T4_h6)
